events.summary: David Bowie did not actually record a soundtrack for The Man Who Fell to Earth; the film's music was written and produced by John Phillips.
New York Theater Workshop announces it will stage Lazarus, a musical based on The Man Who Fell to Earth featuring new songs from David Bowie, later in 2015.
David Bowie announces he is co-writing a new stage musical, Lazarus, with playwright Enda Walsh, featuring new songs and inspired by The Man Who Fell to Earth.
Nicolas Roeg’s film The Man Who Fell to Earth, starring David Bowie as Thomas Newton, is rereleased after 40 years.
A review of the Lazarus original cast recording notes that the recording was made the day Bowie's death was announced and includes three previously unreleased songs performed by Bowie himself.
David Bowie is to part-curate an exhibition of his life and work at the Victoria and Albert museum.
David Bowie's death was announced, prompting tributes including from David Cameron.
David Bowie's death at the age of 69 was confirmed by his son Duncan Jones and on his official Facebook and Twitter presences.
David Bowie turns 60, coinciding with the 30th-anniversary DVD release of The Man Who Fell to Earth.
David Bowie announces the release of Five Years 1969-1973, the first in a series of career-spanning box sets.
A new David Bowie EP, No Plan, was released to mark what would have been the star's 70th birthday, and a charity concert was held at Brixton Academy.

David Bowie's former band members and collaborators are to perform a tribute concert at Brixton Academy on what would have been his 70th birthday, with further shows planned in New York, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Tokyo.
David Bowie released the single "Where Are We Now?" on iTunes on his 66th birthday, marking his return to music.
David Bowie's family said they are overwhelmed by the reaction to his death and are making arrangements for a private ceremony to celebrate his memory.
David Bowie released a new single, "Where Are We Now?", on his 66th birthday, ahead of his first new album in 10 years.
David Bowie announces that he will release his new album Blackstar on his 69th birthday, with a single of the same name preceding it on 2015-11-20.

David Bowie's album The Next Day, released the previous week, went straight to No 1 on iTunes and was likely to become his first No 1 album in the official UK charts since 1993, while advance ticket sales for the V&A exhibition David Bowie Is broke museum records.
A spokesperson for David Bowie confirmed that his 25th album, Blackstar, will be released on January 8, 2016, with the title single out on November 20, 2015.
David Bowie's 1975 single Golden Years is reissued as an iPhone app allowing fans to remix the song.
A new ebook titled "Bowie: A life reviewed" was released, telling David Bowie's ever-changing story as reported by the Guardian and the Observer.
An exhibition titled "David Bowie Is," featuring unprecedented access to the David Bowie archive, premieres at the Australian Centre for the Moving Image in Melbourne and runs until 1 November.
The Victoria and Albert Museum's David Bowie exhibition opened its doors at the Groninger Museum in the Netherlands for fans to view and sign a book of condolence following Bowie's death at age 69.

The Australian Centre for the Moving Image keeps its gallery open late on Thursday and Friday nights in celebration of the David Bowie Is exhibition, with a rotating roster of DJs on Thursdays and occasional Strange Fascination talks.
Around 400 artworks and other items once owned by the late David Bowie go on free public display at Sotheby's in London before being sold in three auctions later in November.
The V&A announces the first museum retrospective of David Bowie, titled "David Bowie is," scheduled to run from 23 March to 28 July 2013.
A specially curated Berlin version of the David Bowie Is exhibition, focusing on Bowie's cathartic years in divided Berlin, opens at the Martin-Gropius-Bau.
David Bowie's new album reached No 1 in its first week of release, his first time topping the albums chart in 20 years.
An exhibition of Brian Duffy's David Bowie photographs opens at Leeds' White Cloth Gallery.
The David Bowie Is exhibition runs at the Martin-Gropius-Bau in Berlin until this date.
David Bowie's style legacy and cultural influence are discussed, including his collaborations with designer Kansai Yamamoto and impact on fashion, but no single main topic-related event is reported.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Dozens of paintings, sculptures and design pieces from David Bowie's art collection go on display in Los Angeles as part of a global tour before Sotheby's auctions the entire collection in London in November.

A new David Bowie box set, Who Can I Be Now?, compiling unreleased material, remastered albums, and live recordings from his 1974–76 American phase, is announced for release on 23 September.
A David Bowie Prom tribute concert was held, featuring reworked Bowie songs performed by various artists.
A plaque commemorating David Bowie's time living in Berlin was unveiled in the city's Schöneberg district.
Nicolas Roeg’s film The Man Who Fell to Earth, starring David Bowie as Thomas Newton, is rereleased after 40 years.

Dozens of paintings, sculptures and design pieces from David Bowie's art collection go on display in Los Angeles as part of a global tour before Sotheby's auctions the entire collection in London in November.

A review is published of the box set David Bowie: Who Can I Be Now? (1974-1976), which traces Bowie's career from Diamond Dogs to Station to Station and includes The Gouster, a reconstruction of an early version of Young Americans.
Three new David Bowie songs from the Lazarus musical were released, recorded with the same band and producer as Blackstar.
An album featuring David Bowie's final recordings, Lazarus Cast Album, is released.
An album featuring the last studio recordings made by David Bowie goes on sale this week, ahead of the opening of the Lazarus stage show next month.
A review of the Lazarus original cast recording notes that the recording was made the day Bowie's death was announced and includes three previously unreleased songs performed by Bowie himself.
Michael C Hall brings David Bowie's musical Lazarus, featuring new songs and classic tracks spanning Bowie's career, to London with previews beginning at the new Kings Cross theatre.
Around 400 artworks and other items once owned by the late David Bowie go on free public display at Sotheby's in London before being sold in three auctions later in November.
BBC2 announces a documentary, David Bowie: The Last Five Years, exploring Bowie’s final projects and featuring previously unheard vocals and unseen archive footage, to be broadcast in January.
The first items from David Bowie's personal art collection were sold at auction in London, fetching more than £24m.
Sydney's New Year's Eve midnight fireworks display included a tribute honoring David Bowie, along with Prince and Gene Wilder.
A new David Bowie EP, No Plan, was released to mark what would have been the star's 70th birthday, and a charity concert was held at Brixton Academy.
A David Bowie tribute concert celebrating his 70th birthday was held, featuring his backing musicians, collaborators, and friends performing his songs.
A one-man show inspired by David Bowie, "From Ibiza to the Norfolk Broads," is performed at the Arts Centre in Swindon.
A graphic novel titled "Haddon Hall: When David Invented Bowie" by Nejib, depicting David Bowie's life at Haddon Hall from 1969 to 1972, is reviewed.
A concert film documenting David Bowie's retirement of his Ziggy Stardust alter ego at the Hammersmith Apollo in 1973 is rereleased into cinemas for a single-night show.
Royal Mail issues a set of 10 postage stamps commemorating David Bowie, featuring six album covers and four tours.

A follow-up to the 1986 film Labyrinth, which starred the late David Bowie as the Goblin King, is in the works, with Fede Alvarez set to write and direct and Bowie's character not expected to feature.

Two limited-edition releases of unreleased David Bowie material, the live album Cracked Actor (Live in Los Angeles 1974) and the 1971 promo album Bowpromo, are set to be issued for the 10th anniversary of Record Store Day.

David Bowie was honoured with three commemorative blue plaques, including one outside the Soho studios where he recorded Hunky Dory and The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars, as part of BBC Music Day.
Six signed photographs of David Bowie taken by his friend Geoff MacCormack in the 1970s are to be auctioned at Bonhams in London.
James Murphy said that David Bowie convinced him to re-form LCD Soundsystem after they split up in 2011.
Former Queen roadie Peter Hince revealed that David Bowie and Queen recorded a batch of songs together that were never released.
Simon Goddard's book Ziggyology, a social history of David Bowie's Ziggy Stardust persona, is reviewed.
David Bowie did not curate the V&A's 2013 retrospective exhibition, though he made his private collection available to its curators.
A BBC4 documentary about the making of David Bowie's album and the birth of his Ziggy Stardust alter ego aired, featuring interviews with collaborators and admirers but not Bowie himself.
David Bowie was described as the quintessential 1970s artist, a lightning rod and mirror for the decade's anxieties, in a retrospective article.

David Bowie made several legendary US TV appearances, including performances on Soul Train in 1975, Bing Crosby's Merrie Old Christmas in 1977, Saturday Night Live in 1979, The Tonight Show in 1980, and The Concert for New York City in 2001.
The Brit Awards are rumored to feature a David Bowie tribute from a supergroup including Damon Albarn, Bono, Noel Gallagher, Adele and Coldplay.
A new ebook titled "Bowie: A life reviewed" was released, telling David Bowie's ever-changing story as reported by the Guardian and the Observer.
Article discusses David Bowie's literary influences and legacy as a writer, with no single main topic-related event.
David Bowie did not actually record a soundtrack for The Man Who Fell to Earth; the film's music was written and produced by John Phillips.
David Bowie's song Space Oddity and its fictional astronaut Major Tom are listed as the top entry in a ranking of the 10 best astronauts.
A teenage David Bowie was among the artists who first found regular audiences at Eel Pie Island, a venue now being celebrated with a museum dedicated to its role in British R&B history.
The "David Bowie Is" exhibition arrives in Australia at the Australian Centre for the Moving Image in Melbourne, though Bowie himself is not expected to attend.
